corpus.note: Maintainers' AI corpus at repo data/write-like-me/ai-generated: 30 machine-generated documents — 22 pieces plus one email thread in eight stage files — (GPT, Claude Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, Gemini Pro/Flash/Thinking) across five registers. Second extraction, 2026-09-09 (first: 2026-08-31): every document re-read in full; all-star_gemini-flash.md and theia-notebooks_haiku.md were regenerated before this run, so their quotes and counts are new. Vetting is provenance (generator per document, on the maintainers' word); `measure --vet` flags presentations_gemini (ai_vocabulary 24.8/1k) and generating-code_gemini-thinking (label_lead 22.3/1k) as outliers on the machine markers, which is expected of Gemini output and no reason to drop them. The email thread is a two-model roleplay, marked co-authored; the 2026-09-09 review round split it into eight files, one per stage of the conversation (introduction, scoping, kickoff preparation, kickoff recap, UI design and the dev-environment incident, language design, editor polish and AI context, wrap-up), because a compilation kept as one file leaves rows scoped to it at tier 3 (technique.md, Step 1). Register balance: article carries 49% of the words, email 22% in the eight files of one thread; register_weights {article: 4, report: 2, social: 2, abstract: 2, email: 1} set on this finished DB so that no single document defines a fifth of every rate and the three-document registers processing targets most (social, abstract, report) count equally, with article, 13 documents from 7 generators, still the largest share (36%). Weights move `rate` only; range, spread, coverage and tiers stay word-count based (db-schema.md). Judged rows were re-counted under written rules: imperative = one per run of two or more consecutive reader-addressed imperative sentences; repetition = one per anaphora run of three or more consecutive sentences or paragraph openers sharing a frame (question volleys and imperative runs go to their own rows); enthusiasm = one per email reply or social post that opens by praising or validating the previous message, or an exclamatory launch; closer-type = 1 per piece (per post or abstract in a multi-piece file) that ends on a punchline, title echo or call to action; fragment = one per verbless or subjectless prose sentence; candor-claim = one per sentence announcing the text's own honesty. Prompt provenance (plainly- vs. style-prompted) was not recorded at generation time and remains an open item.
